findings.title: A duplicate-ID second entry is "not in rules_open" and therefore ACCOUNTED under the partition's own definition — rows 3/4 would carry it before row 5 is reached
findings.recommendation: Cell-by-cell against the parser: a second Decisions entry with an already-used ID is a `key_defects` duplicate, EXCLUDED from `rules_total` and never placed in `rules_open`. Under "a live rule is ACCOUNTED exactly when it is NOT in `rules_open`" and rows tested in order, that entry is a live rule (row 1 fails), not in `rules_open` (row 2 fails), hence accounted — so row 3 or 4 carries its content before row 5 (`key_defects`) is ever tested. Two repairs, take both: move the `key_defects` row to FIRST position (an entry whose ID is in `key_defects` is disposed of before any other row is tested), and define ACCOUNTED as "counted in `rules_total` AND not in `rules_open`" so the definition alone excludes it. Update the design's D-rc13c-4 text and task 3.3's row order to match.

findings.title: The pre-move grep checks "every BOUNDED entry" — but a BOUNDED entry on a non-live owner is deliberately NOT carried (row 1), so the check fails on exactly the history the table permits
findings.recommendation: Scope the record paragraph's pre-move grep to row-4 entries only: "every BOUNDED entry the table sent to row 4 (a live, accounted rule)". A superseded rule that kept a BOUNDED entry (the shape rc13a's own D-bcs history has) would otherwise fail a check whose purpose is to catch a missed carry, not to re-carry history. Mirror the scoping in task 3.3's grep sentence.

findings.title: The precedence scenario's "Regenerate from explore → concluded check → refuse" path has no task: 1.1 adds the header read to the resolve-mode sub-step only
findings.recommendation: The delta's `A concluded staging directory beside an active change` scenario (and the requirement's PRECEDENCE clause (1)) says that after the conflict prompt's "Regenerate from explore" choice the concluded check runs and refuses. Task 1.1 places the check in sub-step 3 (Resolve mode) and says nothing about the conflict sub-step's Regenerate branch, which in the body today proceeds straight to "overwrite the existing change directory". Add to 1.1: the Regenerate option's text gains one sentence — "then the resolve-mode check runs; a concluded staging file is refused here too" — and task 1.3's position assertion checks that sentence sits inside sub-step 2.

findings.title: The record's D-rc13c-4 row says "the decision table verbatim", but the delta carries the partition rewritten at the external walk, not the exploration's table
findings.recommendation: The row's shape claim is false as written: `explore.md`'s D-rc13c-4 domain table (closure token × owner state, five rows, not a partition) is NOT what the ADDED requirement carries — the delta's table is the revised partition (two facts, five rows in test order, `key_defects` and 'accounted' defined by pointer). This is the mapping's first execution, so the record must be exact: reword to "the decision table as REVISED at the external walk (a normative TABLE shape; the exploration's table was superseded by the partition — see the amended D-rc13c-4)" and keep the token column reading DERIVED with a note that the derivation was amended.

findings.recommendation: The readout already resolves this case (first in file order, with a note — `orbit-run-summary-emit`'s maturity requirement and the parser's recovery rule). Add five words: "the live CONCLUDED entry's slot (first in file order when two carry one, as the readout resolves it)" so propose and the readout name the same trigger.

commentary:
This pass read the two surfaces the external walk rewrote — the partition table and the Step 0 precedence — cell by cell against the parser's actual state model rather than against the prose that describes it, which is where the one substantive finding came from: the partition's definition of ACCOUNTED ("not in `rules_open`") is exactly right for every entry the parser COUNTS and exactly wrong for the one kind it excludes from counting, the duplicate-ID second entry, which is neither open nor counted and so falls through to the carrier rows before the key-defects row can catch it. That is the same failure class the external pass named — a partition that is not one — one cell smaller, and it survived because the repair reasoned about `rules_open`'s five states and did not re-read what `rules_total` excludes. The pre-move grep has the mirror-image defect: it was written before the table had a history row and now contradicts it. Both are repairs, not descopes.

The remaining findings are the residue two rapid walks leave behind: a record row whose shape claim predates the table it describes, a Risks figure that Context outgrew, a garbled fragment, a task under the wrong heading, a task that does not reach one branch of a scenario the same walk added. None of them is mechanism. What I probed hardest: every row of the partition against `explore-rules.ts`'s join (open states, the excluded duplicate, orphans, the non-live owner with and without an entry); the three Step 0 scenarios' WHEN clauses for disjointness (they are disjoint now — the conflict scenario is the only one whose WHEN does not name the header, which is correct because precedence (1) fires before the header is read); every scenario in the delta against a task; the delta's pointer discipline (`ask nothing else` and the table header row both absent; the residual stated once; the identifier rule and the state set pointed at); and the mirror-corollary coverage (section list, decision table, shape list all under task 2.4). What I could not do that an independent reader could: unlearn the two walks. I wrote every line under review except the two reviewers' findings, and an in-context pass over rewritten mechanism is the weakest slot in this cadence by design; the record says so rather than the tail.
